newsitem.title: USA: Florida sets up separate NERC power region.
newsitem.headline: Florida sets up separate NERC power region.

text.p: The Florida subregion of the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) has become its own region, separate from SERC, under the North American Electric Reliability Council (NERC) jurisdiction, a NERC spokesman said Tuesday.
"The Florida subregion voted to become a separate regional reliability council at a NERC trustees council meeting this morning," NERC spokesman Gene Gorzelnik said Tuesday.
The new region, to be called the Florida Reliability Coordinating Council (FRCC), will comprise most of the state, excluding the northwestern Florida Panhandle.
That part of the state which receives its electricity from the Gulf Power Co, a subsidiary of Southern Co, will remain part of the SERC region, Gorzelnik said.
"They (the Florida Reliability Coordinating Council) felt it would serve their purposes better being a separate region," Gorzelnik said.
The vote on the Florida separation came at a meeting earlier today in St Louis, Mo., the spokesman said.
The addition of Florida will bring to 10 the number of NERC regions in the U.S.

NERC, a self-governing industry group, was created in 1968 to ensure reliable electricity service throughout the country after a major power outage blacked out cities on the East Coast in November, 1965.
